title: Adding one simplex gives a covering of semi-representable Hom objects
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $K$ a hypercover of $X$ in the category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of semi-representable objects over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. Let $U\subseteq V$ be a simplicial subset of a simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with $U_n$, $V_n$ finite and nonempty for all $n\geq0$ and with $U$ and $V$ having finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Suppose there are $n\geq0$ and $x\in V_n$, $x\notin U_n$, such that (1) $V_i=U_i$ for $i<n$, (2) $V_n=U_n\cup\{x\}$, and (3) every $z\in V_j$ with $j>n$ and $z\notin U_j$ is degenerate. Then the restriction morphism $\operatorname{Hom}(V,K)_0\to\operatorname{Hom}(U,K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object] is a covering in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object].

source.place: Lemma 01GM (lemma-one-more-simplex), statement and proof (via simplicial.tex Lemmas 018R, 017N, 018V)

proof.text: *Gluing the new simplex.* Let $\Delta[n]$ be the simplicial set of order-preserving maps $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$, $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$ the simplicial subset of the non-surjective ones, and $a:\Delta[n]\to V$, $a(\varphi)=V(\varphi)(x)$. Conditions (1)-(3) of the statement are those of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-glue-simplex], so $a$ maps $\partial\Delta[n]$ into $U$, and with $b:\partial\Delta[n]\to U$ the restriction of $a$ the square ($b$, $a$, $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$, $U\subseteq V$) is a pushout of simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $n=0$, $\partial\Delta[0]$ is empty (every map $[m]\to[0]$ is surjective) and $V$ with the inclusion of $U$ and $a$ is a coproduct $U\amalg\Delta[0]$. In Lean apply SSet.glue_simplex with the upper subcomplex equal to top, and transport its result through Subcomplex.topIso V. The naturality of yonedaEquiv identifies the simplex map with the original x.

source.place: Lemma 01GM (lemma-one-more-simplex), proof, first sentence ('V = U amalg Delta[0]') and second paragraph ('By Simplicial, Lemma 018R we have V = U amalg_{boundary Delta[n]} Delta[n]')

proof.text: *Notation and the Hom objects involved.* Call a simplicial set admissible if all its sets of $m$-simplices are finite and nonempty and it has finitely many nondegenerate simplices; $U$ and $V$ are admissible by hypothesis, $\Delta[n]$ is admissible for every $n\geq0$ and $\partial\Delta[n]$ for $n\geq1$ by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-standard-simplex](a),(b). Write $H(S)=\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object] and, for a morphism $f:S\to S'$ of admissible simplicial sets, $f^*:H(S')\to H(S)$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-pushout]; the morphism to be shown a covering is $\rho=\iota^*:H(V)\to H(U)$, $\iota:U\subseteq V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-standard-simplex](a) there is a unique isomorphism $\varepsilon:K_n\to H(\Delta[n])$ with $u^{\Delta[n]}_\varphi\circ\varepsilon=K(\varphi)$ for all $\varphi$ (both are $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta[n],K)_0$, unique up to unique isomorphism). Obtain a representing boundary family from lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-exists, converting its unique-map formulation into Functor.IsRepresentedBy by Function.bijective_iff_existsUnique.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, second paragraph (the objects Hom(Delta[n],K)_0, Hom(boundary Delta[n],K)_0)

proof.text: Every split epimorphism f of formal coproducts is a covering: for each target index j, a section g provides an index g(j) above j and a component factorization of the identity through the f-component. Hence the generated covering sieve contains the identity, so is top. Apply this to an isomorphism and its inverse. By lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-covering-permanence, composing a covering with an isomorphism is a covering.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, second paragraph ('this arrow is identified with K_n -> (cosk_{n-1} sk_{n-1} K)_n and hence is a covering'): the identification is by isomorphisms, which preserve coverings

proof.text: *Case $n\geq1$: the fibre square.* By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-pushout](a), applied to $A=\partial\Delta[n]$, $B=U$, $C=\Delta[n]$, $D=V$ with $p=b$, $q$ the inclusion $j:\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$ (all four admissible by step 2), $H(V)$ with $\rho$ and $a^*$ is a fibre product of $b^*:H(U)\to H(\partial\Delta[n])$ and $j^*:H(\Delta[n])\to H(\partial\Delta[n])$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$. Use K_n itself as the simplex Hom object, with the universal family given by simplicial_hom_standard_simplex. The arrow H(V) to K_n is evaluation of the V-family at x; its projection equations are exactly the family compatibility equations. The arrow H(U) to the boundary Hom object is the inverse representing bijection applied to the U-family pulled back along b.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, second paragraph ('By Simplicial, Lemma 017N we get that ... is a fibre product square')

proof.text: Obtain the boundary comparison isomorphism theta and boundary restriction rho from simplicial_hom_boundary_matching, with rho followed by theta equal to the matching map mu_n. Thus rho = mu_n followed by theta inverse, so it is a covering by the hypercover hypothesis and step 3. Its component equations identify it with the qStar needed by the Hom pushout lemma.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, last two sentences ('By Simplicial, Lemma 018V this arrow is identified with K_n -> (cosk_{n-1} sk_{n-1} K)_n and hence is a covering by definition of a hypercovering')

proof.text: For any pullback square with a covering bottom arrow g, covering permanence gives a covering canonical pullback projection. The comparison isoPullback from the given square to the canonical pullback identifies the top arrow with that projection after an isomorphism. Apply composition permanence and step 3. This proves the target restriction is a covering in positive degree.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, second paragraph ('Thus it suffices to show that the bottom horizontal arrow is a covering'), with hypercovering.tex Lemma 01G4 (lemma-covering-permanence) (2) for the base change

proof.text: For n=0, boundary_zero identifies the boundary with the empty subcomplex. The same glued-simplex pushout, together with simplicialHomObject_pushout_empty_isProduct, makes the V-Hom object a product of the U-Hom object and K_0, with projection to K_0 given by evaluation at x. FormalCoproduct.isTerminalIncl applied to the terminal etale object id_X proves M_0(K) terminal. IsPullback.of_is_product converts the product to a pullback over M_0(K); its bottom arrow is definitionally the zero matching map, a covering by hK 0. Apply step 6. Finally case analysis on the natural number n combines zero and successor degrees.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, first paragraph ('If n = 0 ... V = U amalg Delta[0]. In this case Hom(V,K)_0 = Hom(U,K)_0 x K_0. The result, in this case, then follows from Lemma 01G4')

proof_origin.place: Lemma 01GM (lemma-one-more-simplex), proof, formalized by R3 from the existing glue, standard-simplex, boundary-matching, Hom-existence, Hom-pushout and covering-permanence statements; comparison maps and isomorphism coverings are proved locally.

split_report.summary: Proof written from Stacks 01GM. The source's three citations became nodes: 018R (glue one simplex: V = U amalg_{boundary} Delta[n]) -> lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-glue-simplex; 017N (Hom(-,K)_0 turns the pushout into a fibre product, plus the product case over an empty A needed for n = 0) -> lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-pushout; 018V with 0177 (Hom(Delta[n],K)_0 = K_n, Hom(boundary,K)_0 = M_n(K), restriction = mu_n) -> lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-standard-simplex, stated against the explicit matching object M_n(K) of def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object instead of cosk_{n-1}sk_{n-1}. Written out what the source leaves implicit: that isomorphisms of SR(X) are coverings (so the identifications preserve coverings), the base change through the canonical fibre product of lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits and covering permanence (1),(2), and the n = 0 case through the final object. Statement unchanged (it assumes V also has finitely many nondegenerate simplices, which the source does not need but which follows from (1)-(3)). No Lean on slopmaster2.
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the fourth paragraph of lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-refinement's proof ('Previously chosen faces prescribe compatible boundaries; the matching covers of U lift those boundaries after finite refinement') for one new simplex: step 1 and 4 the prescribed boundary (gluing along boundary Delta[n]), steps 5-6 the lift along the matching cover K_n -> M_n(K) by base change, step 7 the degree-0 case.
